solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Clue to patients’ accommodation problem

blocks.note: surface reading: a hint about where hospital patients are housed
setter's reading: the answer, split into two words, is an instruction which turns it into a hospital room for patients

explanation.surface: A puzzle hint about a hospital's shortage of beds.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as DRAW BACK: drawing WARD back gives DRAW, so the answer is itself a clue to a ward, the room where patients stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a disadvantage or snag, a common everyday synonym for a problem.

clue.text: A case of Garland’s last musical making a comeback

indicators.note: last tells us to keep only the final letter of the singer's name
a comeback is a return, so the show's title is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the final letter of Judy Garland's surname
the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón

explanation.surface: A tale of Judy Garland's final musical returning to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A case' looks like an example, but it is the definition: the dative is a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the dative is the noun case marking an indirect object, as in Latin or German.

clue.text: Exact payment for archdeacon’s time touring

indicators.note: touring means going all round something, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: an age is a long period of time
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: Demanding precise payment for a church dignitary's travelling time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exact' looks like an adjective meaning precise; here it is a verb, to extract payment, which is what revenge does.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to take revenge for it, to make someone pay for the injury done.

clue.text: Tiny animal reserve close to small river

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: to book something is to reserve it
the final letter of small
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A small creature lives in a reserve by a little river.
explanation.definitionFit: A booklouse is a minute wingless insect found among old papers and books, so a tiny animal.

clue.text: Doctor clears them around hotel in case a nut goes inside

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged
around says the rearranged letters surround the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A doctor tidies people up around a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Nut is slang for the head, so the definition is a protective case that a head goes into.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash helmet is protective headgear worn by motorcyclists, a hard shell that the wearer's head sits within.

clue.text: Extravagant high-five!

definitions.note: a phrase for the action rather than a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: lavish, as of a big celebratory meal
second meaning: read literally, a slap delivered upwards, palm to palm

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the playful literal reading of the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a lavish, generous one; a high-five is literally hands slapped together raised overhead.

clue.text: Creamy mixture tipped on a sponge

indicators.note: tipped means turned over, so in a down entry the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a fool is a dessert of fruit folded into cream
taken as written

explanation.surface: A creamy concoction spilt onto a bath sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of puréed fruit and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is the fibrous dried pod of a gourd used as a bath sponge for scrubbing.

clue.text: Minister mostly collects tax for servicemen

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped
to collect is to gather in, so the shortened word holds the other piece

blocks.note: a priest is a minister of religion
VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: A government minister gathers taxes to pay for the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks political, but it is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Privates are soldiers of the lowest rank, the ordinary servicemen of an army.

clue.text: Spectacle that moves around is promised land

indicators.note: around says the first piece encloses the short word that follows

blocks.note: a parade is a public show that processes along
taken as written

explanation.surface: A moving procession reaches the land of promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is heaven or an ideal place, the land of bliss promised to the faithful.

clue.text: Dry European drink in greenish-blue

indicators.note: in places the letter and the drink inside the colour word

blocks.note: teal is a greenish-blue colour
E is the abbreviation for European
a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A European sipping a drink while feeling green about the gills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' here means alcohol-free, as in a dry state, not lacking water.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotal person abstains completely from alcohol, which is what dry means of people or places.

clue.text: Office equipment that is right next to PC

indicators.note: next to says the abbreviations are placed alongside the police officer

blocks.note: a PC, police constable, is a cop
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A printer that sits beside the office computer.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a personal computer, which suits office equipment, but it is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier, or photocopier, is a standard machine in offices for duplicating documents.

clue.text: Watch heads of government in lectures on sex

indicators.note: heads are the tops, so the first letter of each word is taken
in an across entry, on means placed after, so the earlier phrase goes second

blocks.note: sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals
the initial letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Keeping an eye on politicians who lecture about sex.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' puts A after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of staying awake to keep watch, for instance overnight beside the sick.

clue.text: Disorganised leader to host a quiet venture

indicators.note: the leader is what goes in front, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of host
taken as written
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
to hazard is to venture or risk

explanation.surface: A boss plans to put on a low-key business venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader to host' looks like a chief giving a party; it means the first letter of host.
explanation.definitionFit: Haphazard means lacking any order or plan, which is to say random and disorganised.

clue.text: Travelling to Peru in car from San Juan?

indicators.note: travelling means on the move, so these letters shift into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone driving to Peru from a Latin American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: San Juan is the capital of Puerto Rico; the question mark shows it is one example of where such a person comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from San Juan, the island's capital city, is by example a native of Puerto Rico.

clue.text: Cut down on Geordie sides to suppress incompetence

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two outer letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: to cut down on something is to use less of it
a Geordie comes from Newcastle in the North East, NE
the first and last letters of suppress

explanation.surface: Reducing Newcastle's football teams to stamp out poor performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppress' looks like the verb of the sentence, but only its outside letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Uselessness is the state of being of no use or ability, the quality of being incompetent.

clue.text: Power over Lancashire? That makes me smile

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: a say is power or influence, as in having a say
Lancashire is a crumbly English cheese

explanation.surface: Someone smiling at the idea of power over a northern county.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England, but also gives its name to a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers tell subjects to say cheese because the word stretches the mouth into a grin.

clue.text: Singular couples taking in little darlings

indicators.note: taking in means admitting, so the letters before it enclose the small word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for singular
to couple is to join together, as ties do
wee is Scots for little

explanation.surface: Odd pairs of parents bring in their little darlings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little darlings' reads as one phrase, but little supplies letters and darlings alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetie is an affectionate term of address, like darling, for a loved one.

clue.text: Request that God divides wealth

indicators.note: to divide something is to split it, so the deity's name goes into the middle

blocks.note: a plea is an urgent request
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A prayer that a deity will share out riches.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an abundance or excess, and wealth can mean a large plentiful amount of something.

clue.text: Comic accepts change to Melchester’s first daydreamer

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of the town is wanted
to accept is to take in, so the comic word holds the rest

blocks.note: comic as an adjective means funny or witty
to alter is to change
the opening letter of Melchester

explanation.surface: A comic book alters the story of Melchester's star player.
explanation.walkthrough: Melchester Rovers is the fictional football club in the British comic strip Roy of the Rovers, which fits the comic surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Mitty is the James Thurber character who lives in heroic fantasies, so his name means a fantasist.

clue.text: Perfect time to interrupt kiss and cuddle

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the single letter goes inside

blocks.note: to spoon is an old word for kissing and cuddling
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The ideal moment to break up a couple's embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on means exactly right or accurate, an informal British word for perfect or precise.

clue.text: Rug to go under end of bureau

indicators.note: end of picks out only the final letter of the furniture word
under in a down clue says the second piece sits below the letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of bureau
to go is a euphemism for urinating, to pee

explanation.surface: A rug that has to be slipped under the desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rug' wants to be a carpet, but it is slang for a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: Rug is humorous slang for a hairpiece, and a toupee is a small wig covering a bald patch.

clue.text: Fan of old farm equipment

blocks.note: ex means former
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: An enthusiast for vintage farm machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan of' looks like an admirer of the old tractors; fan here is the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor fan draws stale air or steam out of a kitchen or bathroom, so extractor names a type of fan.

clue.text: Native American wanting horse with speed

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing from the tribe's name

blocks.note: the Apache are a Native American people
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A Native American without a horse cannot move fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' fits the Western scene, but it is drug slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an adverb meaning quickly or swiftly, so it substitutes for with speed.

clue.text: Big beast in foreign river

blocks.note: in and hip both mean fashionable
the Po is a river in Italy

explanation.surface: A large animal wallowing in a river abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a linking preposition but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus, shortened in speech, is one of the largest land animals in Africa.

clue.text: Line showing pressure of abrasion, endlessly repaired

indicators.note: without ends means both the first and last letters are removed
something repaired has been fixed and put back together, so the letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stress line from an endlessly mended scrape.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map an isobar is a contour joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Twisting cap in hands, check clothes

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so the check word is wrapped around the hands

blocks.note: to check is to halt or stop
hands are workers, a ship's crew

explanation.surface: Someone twisting their cap in their hands, checking their clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' reads as garments, but it is a verb, to dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw top is a lid that is twisted onto a bottle or jar to close it.

clue.text: Part of plant in which stewed meat is tinned?

indicators.note: stewed food has been cooked and stirred, so these letters are mixed
something tinned is sealed inside a can, so the jumbled meat goes into the metal

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant part found in canned stew.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is Sn on the periodic table, from the Latin stannum.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-producing male organ of a flower, so a part of a plant.

clue.text: Painter needing frames someone locked away

indicators.note: to frame is to surround, so the words before it enclose the answer

blocks.note: found inside these two words

explanation.surface: An artist who needs picture frames for a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' and 'frames' suggest picture framing; the frame is the outside of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is a person confined or detained, typically in wartime without trial, so locked up.
